decision.rationale:
WHAT I DID
One free transfer: Guéhi (MCI) out, Hill (BOU, £5.6m) in. No hit, no chip. Calvert-Lewin is captain for Leeds v COV(h), with N.Jackson (ips(a)) as vice.

WHAT I LEARNED
Everything I found came from line-ups and reports of the 21 Nov matches.
- Guéhi pulled out of England duty with a hip problem on 13 Nov, but he started at centre-back for City in the 1-1 with Fulham. I raised his minutes from 54 to 80. That makes him look better, not worse, but his projection is still low.
- Haaland started that game and had a goal disallowed. He stays at 90 minutes.
- Hill and Tavernier both started in Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Forest, and Hill was involved in a goal. Hill is in the team, so the player we are buying is checked.
- Arsenal drew 2-2 at Newcastle. Gabriel, Konsa, Rice and Ødegaard all started. Saliba was on the bench, which is a fitness return to watch. I set Konsa to 75 minutes as a rotation risk and Gabriel to 90.
- N.Jackson started as the lone striker in Villa's 0-0 with Sunderland. I set him to 85 minutes.
- Tzolakis started and was excellent in Hull's 2-0 win over Brighton, so he is in the team.
- A predicted Leeds line-up has Calvert-Lewin and Muharemović starting against Coventry. That is only a tier-3 source.
I ran out of searches before checking Brighton (Groß, Vuskovic, Verbruggen), Man Utd (Mbeumo), Brentford (Lewis-Potter) and Coventry. None of them is bought or sold this week.

Still unsure:
- Konsa's place now that Saliba is back.
- Whether the starting eleven, which the solver re-picks, starts Konsa over a fit bench option. Last week's review warned against exactly that.

WHY THIS PLAN
After my adjustments, Plan 4 is only 0.6 ahead of rolling (plan 5). On its own that is within the noise, and normally I would roll. But the rolling plan makes this exact move next week anyway: its path sells Guéhi for Hill in GW13. So this is the same transfer a week early, with nothing lost in banked transfers. Hill is checked and has Fulham away. Guéhi has Arsenal away, a recent hip problem, and a 6-week projection of only about 12.7. Hill is also being heavily bought (about 94k), so he may cost more by the deadline.
I turned down plans 6 and 7. Taking a hit to swap Rice for Ødegaard, or Lewis-Potter for Rudoni, scores 2.6 to 6.1 points worse than rolling, and nothing I found makes either swap urgent. The solver plans Rice to Ødegaard as a free transfer next week.
No chip: the triple captain's gain this week (+5.3) is below its 7.0 bar, and the solver is saving it for GW19. The free hit is far below its bar, the wildcard projects negative, and the bench boost isn't available.
